reference_summary: At 06:20:10, Synthetic Harbor control closed feeder breaker 12-F4 to restore Synthetic Cedar Feeder after upstream fault clearing. Primary cause: active relay setting group B specified 280 A phase pickup instead of correct 600 A primary pickup. A stale maintenance file left setting group B active after 04:45 testing, while group A held the normal 600 A pickup. At 06:20:12, the feeder relay issued a phase time-overcurrent trip after 0.5 s delay at 1.46 times pickup. Impact: Synthetic Cedar Feeder outage lasted 38 minutes, interrupting 7.84 MW at 0.92 power factor and 12 kV. Mitigation: at 06:52:40, operators switched relay 12-F4 from group B to group A with 600 A phase pickup.

reference_summary: At 08:55:12, Synthetic Summit control closed recloser R-7 to restore Synthetic Birch Feeder after a circuit fault cleared. Primary cause: the recloser control's active group C specified 40 A ground pickup rather than the intended 90 A primary value. A firmware profile upload at 07:30:45 activated group C, while group A retained the normal 90 A ground pickup. At 08:55:15, the recloser control initiated a ground trip after 0.4 s, opening R-7 and stopping restoration. Impact: Synthetic Birch Feeder restoration was delayed 46 minutes, from 08:55 to 09:41, before successful re-energization. Mitigation: at 09:41:05, crews corrected the recloser control from ground pickup 40 A to the intended 90 A primary value.
title: Recloser control setting discrepancy delays Synthetic Summit Feeder restoration

reference_summary: At 03:14:22.500 UTC, transmission frequency fell to 59.91 hertz, crossing the 59.95 hertz reserve activation threshold. The Synthetic Grid Coordination Center issued an 80 megawatt reserve activation command at 03:14:23.000 UTC. Primary cause: at 03:14:10 UTC, a maintenance script reloaded the station Ethernet switch, causing 2.6 seconds of SCADA telemetry queueing. At 03:14:25.100 UTC, the battery inverter actually ramped to 80 megawatts, but the controller-indicated value remained stale. Frequency nadir reached 59.82 hertz at 03:14:24.900 UTC, lower than the 59.85 hertz pre-event projection. At 03:27:00 UTC, operators bypassed the affected switch, restoring telemetry latency to 85 milliseconds.

reference_summary: At 10:07:12.300 UTC, system frequency dropped to 59.89 hertz, exceeding the 59.95 hertz reserve activation threshold. The Synthetic Kestrel Hydro Reserve received a 120 megawatt activation order at 10:07:12.900 UTC from the coordination center. Primary cause: a 10:05:00 UTC firmware update enabled verbose diagnostic logging on the RTU, saturating its serial processor for 3.2 seconds. SCADA displayed the last pre-event hydro output of 0 megawatts until 10:07:16.100 UTC despite actual generation starting. Frequency nadir reached 59.78 hertz at 10:07:14.900 UTC, and underfrequency load shedding stage one operated at 59.80 hertz. At 10:12:00 UTC, technicians disabled verbose RTU logging, restoring telemetry latency from 3.2 seconds to 180 milliseconds.
title: Synthetic Kestrel Hydro Reserve Telemetry Delay Incident 20260910

reference_summary: At 10:14:02.100, the upstream Synthetic North Feeder breaker opened and isolated Synthetic Harbor Microgrid from the grid. The battery inverter anti-islanding active frequency shift was disabled in commissioning profile B, leaving only passive overfrequency and underfrequency thresholds. After island formation, the 2.0 MW generation exceeded the 1.85 MW load, so frequency rose slowly from 60.00 Hz at 10:14:02.500. The point of common coupling remained energized until 10:14:05.600, causing a 3.500-second islanding detection delay beyond the 2.000-second limit. Operators enabled battery inverter active frequency shift and reduced the overfrequency trip threshold from 61.20 Hz to 60.80 Hz on 2026-09-10.

reference_summary: At 14:22:10.000, the Synthetic East Loop Feeder breaker opened and left Synthetic Larkspur Microgrid serving its local load. The voltage vector shift relay threshold was set to 15.0 degrees in configuration C instead of the intended 6.0 degrees. After islanding, the phase angle across the point of common coupling shifted only 6.5 degrees, below the mis-set 15.0-degree vector shift threshold. The microgrid remained islanded until 14:22:14.450, producing a 4.450-second detection delay that exceeded the 2.000-second requirement. Engineers corrected the vector shift threshold to 6.0 degrees and added a 0.250-second confirmation timer to prevent nuisance tripping. At 14:22:10.000, the point of common coupling breaker status changed from closed to open in the supervisory control log.
